problemStatement: The previous reference-model packet correctly found Microsoft Confirmed under the four-family gate, but its two diffusion documents were both Microsoft-published customer stories. The system therefore proves named adoption claims only through a supplier-controlled publication surface, while customer self-disclosures and SEC/IR operating results are not represented as distinct source roles. This Work Item adds an explicit independent-source boundary and updates the diffusion gate so vendor attribution, adopter self-disclosure, and financial/operating corroboration remain separate and auditable.

Changing SEC response limits or rewriting the existing four-family organization, production-system, outcome, or counter-review gate outside the diffusion-source boundary
Treating social posts, supplier marketing, or discovery-only articles as authoritative independent evidence

riskAssessment.reason: Independent diffusion is a hard condition for the product claim. Misclassifying supplier-controlled material as independent could produce a false reference model, while rejecting valid customer disclosures could hide a real industry pattern. The implementation must preserve legacy snapshots, bound cross-origin URLs explicitly, keep provenance classification in Rust, and pass the full hosted lifecycle.

reasons: The Work Item changes source authority semantics, serialized evidence metadata, the highest reference-model gate, and hosted lifecycle evidence.

preReviewWarnings: Supplier-published customer stories must not silently count as independent corroboration; customer self-disclosure and technical attribution remain separate.

acceptance: The runtime distinguishes supplier attribution, independent customer self-disclosure, and discovery-only material with typed source roles; legacy JSON remains readable.
Independent diffusion evidence requires at least two authoritative independent source URIs and named adopters/peers; supplier-only sources do not satisfy the hard condition.
PwC and NIQ customer/IR URLs are collected as explicit bounded independent sources without guessed cross-origin URLs or unbounded crawling.
The report exposes independent diffusion count, supplier attribution count, source-role provenance, and missing proof separately.
TDD covers independent-source promotion, supplier-only suppression, cross-origin URL validation, legacy deserialization, localized rendering, and full gate behavior.
Python and Shell remain orchestration-only; Rust owns provenance classification, evidence metadata, the gate, Stage assignment, and report values.
SEC/IR and customer disclosures remain distinct evidence classes; no causal productivity claim is inferred from a single customer case.
The Contract-bound local checks, strict quality gate, PR checks, hosted CI, merge, and Work Item closure each produce passing evidence before the next lifecycle stage begins.

intent.problem: The prior Microsoft packet's diffusion evidence came from Microsoft-published customer stories. The product needs to distinguish technical attribution from independent customer adoption and operating-result corroboration before calling an AI-era organization a durable industry model.
constraints: Do not weaken the existing four-family gate or convert source quality into a score.
Only explicitly configured bounded URLs may be fetched; cross-origin sources must be declared and validated.
Supplier material may explain technical attribution but cannot satisfy independent diffusion by itself.
Customer self-disclosures and SEC/IR results remain primary for their own claims, not proof of Microsoft's technical implementation.
Python and Shell may orchestrate and verify but may not own provenance classification or reference-model judgment.
The complete repository lifecycle is required: local checks, PR checks, hosted CI, merge, and closure.
intent.rationale: The remaining research risk is not discovery volume; it is provenance semantics. A typed independent-source boundary lets ORG-X retain supplier case studies as attribution while requiring corroboration from the adopters' own disclosures.
